q: The debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' (Plan Head 71), representing the value of the stores held in stock in the depots, forms part of:

options.A: The Block Account of the Railways
options.B: The working expenses of the year
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The Traffic Suspense

e: The debit balance under Stores Suspense represents the value of stores held in stock in the depots, which is an asset of the Railways and forms part of the Block Account.

q: Grants-in-aid made by law by Parliament to the States under Article 275 of the Constitution, for the purposes specified therein, are:

options.A: Voted expenditure of the Union Government
options.B: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India
options.C: Met out of the Public Account of India
options.D: Financed from the Contingency Fund of India

e: Grants-in-aid made to the States under Article 275 for the purposes specified therein are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India and are therefore not voted by Parliament.

q: The Separation Convention of 1924, which separated the finances of the Railways from the general finances of the Government of India, was given effect to through:

options.A: An Act of the British Parliament
options.B: The Government of India Act, 1935
options.C: A resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly
options.D: A notification issued by the Railway Board

e: The Separation Convention of 1924, which separated railway finances from the general finances, was given effect to through a resolution adopted by the Legislative Assembly.

q: The Financial Commissioner (Railways) is:

options.A: An officer of the Ministry of Finance deputed to conduct the audit of the railway accounts
options.B: The head of the Railway Audit organisation
options.C: The Chairman of the Indian Railway Finance Corporation
options.D: A Member of the Railway Board and the principal financial adviser to the Board on matters of railway finance

e: The Financial Commissioner (Railways) is a Member of the Railway Board and the principal financial adviser to the Board on matters of railway finance.

q: Under Article 280 of the Constitution, besides recommending the distribution of the net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States, the Finance Commission also recommends:

options.A: The measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the State
options.B: The disinvestment programme of the Central Government
options.C: The rate of dividend payable by the Railways to General Finances
options.D: The borrowing limits of the public sector undertakings

e: Under Article 280, besides tax distribution, the Finance Commission recommends the measures needed to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement the resources of the Panchayats and the Municipalities in the State.

q: The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement, laid before Parliament along with the Budget under the FRBM Act, 2003, sets out:

options.A: The strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year
options.B: Three-year rolling targets for the specified fiscal indicators
options.C: An assessment of the growth prospects of the economy along with the underlying assumptions
options.D: The expenditure framework for the three years following the Budget year

e: The Fiscal Policy Strategy Statement laid under the FRBM Act sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area for the ensuing financial year; rolling targets belong to the Medium-Term Fiscal Policy Statement.

q: Under Article 117(1) of the Constitution, a Bill or amendment making provision for any of the matters specified in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of Article 110(1):

options.A: Can be introduced in either House of Parliament without any recommendation
options.B: Shall not be introduced or moved except on the recommendation of the President, and shall not be introduced in the Rajya Sabha
options.C: Can be introduced in the Rajya Sabha with the recommendation of the President
options.D: Can be introduced only after the Demands for Grants have been voted

e: Under Article 117(1), a Bill or amendment making provision for matters in sub-clauses (a) to (f) of Article 110(1) can be introduced or moved only on the recommendation of the President, and cannot be introduced in the Rajya Sabha.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Estimates Committee of Parliament:
1. The Committee may suggest alternative policies in order to bring about efficiency and economy in administration.
2. The Committee suggests the form in which the estimates are to be presented to Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the Estimates Committee may suggest alternative policies to bring about efficiency and economy in administration, and it also suggests the form in which the estimates are to be presented to Parliament.

q: The Chairman of the Estimates Committee of Parliament is:

options.A: Elected by the members of the Committee from amongst themselves
options.B: Nominated by the Minister of Parliamentary Affairs
options.C: Appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee
options.D: The senior-most member of the Committee, by convention

e: The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.

q: The salaries and allowances of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are:

options.A: Voted by Parliament every year as part of the Demands for Grants
options.B: Paid out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of the States
options.D: Charged on the Consolidated Fund of India

e: The salaries and allowances of the Chairman and the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha are charged on the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 112(3)(b).

q: The monthly statement rendered by a station to the Traffic Accounts Office, accounting for all the traffic transactions of the station and showing the balance due from the station, is known as the:

options.A: Station Balance Sheet
options.B: Traffic Book
options.C: Account Current
options.D: Cash Remittance Note

e: The Station Balance Sheet is the monthly statement rendered by a station to the Traffic Accounts Office, accounting for all its traffic transactions and showing the balance due from the station.

q: The earnings collected at a station are required to be remitted to the Cash Office or the accredited bank:

options.A: Once a week
options.B: Daily
options.C: Once a fortnight
options.D: At the end of the month

e: Earnings collected at a station are required to be remitted daily to the Cash Office or the accredited bank.

q: Of the assured annual outlay of Rs 20,000 crore under the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), the amount met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 10,000 crore
options.B: Rs 15,000 crore
options.C: Rs 20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 5,000 crore

e:
Working: Of the assured annual RRSK outlay of Rs 20,000 crore, Rs 15,000 crore is met from Gross Budgetary Support, so the amount met from the internal resources of the Railways = 20,000 - 15,000 = Rs 5,000 crore.
Update: the figures in this question describe the original RRSK design (assured outlay Rs 20,000 crore a year: Rs 15,000 crore GBS + Rs 5,000 crore internal resources). RRSK's currency has since been extended for a further five years w.e.f. 2022-23, with total Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 45,000 crore. (Source: Ministry of Railways, Rajya Sabha Unstarred Question No. 138, answered 02.02.2024.)

q: In the Balance Sheet of the Railways, a debit balance outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads is shown:

options.A: On the assets side, as an amount recoverable
options.B: On the liabilities side
options.C: Netted against the Capital-at-charge
options.D: As a footnote, outside the Balance Sheet

e: A debit balance outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads represents an amount recoverable by the Railways and is therefore shown on the assets side of the Balance Sheet.

q: The first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.B: Winter Session
options.C: Special Session
options.D: Monsoon Session

e: The first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the Monsoon Session.

q: The Finance Accounts of the Union Government, in respect of the Ministries and Departments whose accounts are compiled under the departmentalised system of accounting, are compiled by the:

options.A: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.B: Controller General of Accounts
options.C: Reserve Bank of India
options.D: Railway Board

e: For the Ministries and Departments under the departmentalised system of accounting, the Finance Accounts of the Union Government are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts.

q: The principle of 'unity' (comprehensiveness) in Government budgeting requires that:

options.A: The estimates of expenditure are framed in gross terms, without netting off the related receipts
options.B: The authorisation of Parliament to incur expenditure is valid for one financial year only
options.C: All the receipts and expenditure of the Government are presented together in a single unified budget
options.D: The Budget of the Government is balanced every year

e: The principle of unity (comprehensiveness) in budgeting requires that all the receipts and expenditure of the Government are presented together in a single unified budget, rather than in fragmented budgets.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the basis on which appropriations are made to the Depreciation Reserve Fund from the basis of appropriation to the Railway Pension Fund?

options.A: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed on actuarial valuation, whereas appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed on the original cost and codal life of assets
options.B: Both appropriations are assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of the assets concerned
options.C: Appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed with reference to the original cost of the assets and their prescribed (codal) life, whereas the appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed with reference to the actuarial valuation of the pension liability
options.D: Appropriation to the Pension Fund is assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of assets, whereas appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is assessed on actuarial valuation

e: The distinction lies in the basis of assessment: appropriation to the Depreciation Reserve Fund is fixed with reference to the original cost of assets and their prescribed (codal) life, whereas the appropriation to the Pension Fund rests on actuarial valuation of the pension liability.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Safety Fund (RSF) from the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF)?

options.A: The Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund credited mainly with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares and used for works relating to level crossings and road over/under bridges, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund with a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore set up in 2001-02 to wipe out the arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety assets
options.B: The Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund with a corpus of Rs 17,000 crore, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares
options.C: Both the funds are continuing funds credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares
options.D: The Railway Safety Fund is financed entirely by Gross Budgetary Support, whereas the Special Railway Safety Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares

e: The Railway Safety Fund is a continuing fund fed mainly by the safety surcharge on passenger fares, used for level-crossing and road bridge works. The Special Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund of Rs 17,000 crore set up in 2001-02 to clear renewal arrears of over-aged safety assets.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Works Register from the Liability Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Works Register records the commitments incurred against a grant, whereas the Liability Register records the progressive expenditure on each work
options.B: Both registers record the sanctions, allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work
options.C: The Works Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Liability Register is maintained in the Accounts Office
options.D: The Works Register records, work-wise, the sanctions, budget allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work, whereas the Liability Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, against which payments have yet to be made

e: The Works Register records, work-wise, the sanctions, budget allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work, whereas the Liability Register records liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, for which payment has yet to be made.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Suspense Register from the Debt Head Report?

options.A: The Suspense Register shows the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, whereas the Debt Head Report watches the clearance of individual outstanding items
options.B: The Suspense Register is maintained to watch the outstanding items under each suspense head and secure their clearance, whereas the Debt Head Report is a monthly statement showing the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads
options.C: Both the Suspense Register and the Debt Head Report are monthly statements rendered to the Railway Board along with the Account Current
options.D: The Suspense Register is rendered to the Railway Board every month, whereas the Debt Head Report is maintained in the Accounts Office only

e: The Suspense Register is maintained to watch the outstanding items under each suspense head and secure their clearance, whereas the Debt Head Report is a monthly statement showing the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Reserve Bank Suspense' from 'PSB Suspense' in railway accounts?

options.A: Reserve Bank Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with the Reserve Bank of India
options.B: Both heads are operated for transactions with the Reserve Bank of India pending its advice
options.C: Reserve Bank Suspense is operated for transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank of India, pending the Bank's advice, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank, pending settlement or receipt of the bank's advice
options.D: Reserve Bank Suspense represents the cash balance of the Railways with the Reserve Bank, whereas PSB Suspense represents cheques remitted into the bank but not yet realised

e: Reserve Bank Suspense is operated for transactions in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank of India pending the Bank's advice, whereas PSB Suspense is operated for transactions with the accredited public sector bank pending settlement or the bank's advice.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Demands Recoverable' from 'Demands Payable' in railway accounts?

options.A: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for services rendered, pending realisation, are debited to Demands Recoverable, whereas amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to Demands Payable
options.B: Amounts due to the Railways are credited to Demands Recoverable, whereas amounts due by the Railways are debited to Demands Payable
options.C: Both heads record amounts due to the Railways from outside parties
options.D: Demands Recoverable relates to transactions with other railways, whereas Demands Payable relates to transactions with the Railway Board

e: Amounts due to the Railways from outside parties for services rendered, pending realisation, are debited to Demands Recoverable, whereas amounts due by the Railways to outside parties for goods and services received, pending payment, are credited to Demands Payable.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Capital Fund from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Capital Fund is used for passenger amenities and labour welfare works, whereas the Development Fund is used for financing asset-creating capital works
options.B: The Capital Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Development Fund is credited out of the surplus
options.C: Both the funds can be used only for renewal and replacement of existing assets
options.D: The Capital Fund is used mainly for financing asset-creating (capital) works out of the Railways' internal resources, whereas the Development Fund is used for works relating to passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvements, which may not be directly remunerative

e: The Capital Fund is used mainly for financing asset-creating (capital) works out of the Railways' internal resources, whereas the Development Fund is used for passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvements, which may not be directly remunerative.

q: In the Works Programme (Pink Book), which of the following correctly distinguishes 'itemised works' from an 'umbrella work'?

options.A: Itemised works are groups of similar small works provided with a lumpsum provision, whereas an umbrella work is a single work shown individually
options.B: Works costing more than the prescribed limit are shown individually as itemised works, whereas an umbrella work is a group of similar small works provided for together with a lumpsum provision under one head
options.C: Both itemised works and umbrella works are shown individually in the Pink Book
options.D: Itemised works require the sanction of the Railway Board, whereas umbrella works require no sanction at all

e: Works costing more than the prescribed limit are shown individually as itemised works in the Pink Book, whereas an umbrella work is a group of similar small works provided for together with a lumpsum provision under one head.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the monthly Account Current of a zonal railway from the Finance Accounts of the Railways?

options.A: The Account Current is the annual consolidated account of the Railways as a whole, whereas the Finance Accounts are the monthly accounts of the zonal railways
options.B: Both the Account Current and the Finance Accounts are monthly accounts rendered by the zonal railways to the Railway Board
options.C: The Account Current is the monthly account of the receipts and disbursements of a zonal railway rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Finance Accounts are the annual consolidated accounts of the Railways as a whole, compiled by the Railway Board from the Account Currents of the zonal railways and other accounting units
options.D: The Finance Accounts are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas the Account Current is compiled by the Railway Board

e: The Account Current is a zonal railway's monthly account of receipts and disbursements rendered to the Railway Board. The Finance Accounts are the annual consolidated accounts of the Railways as a whole, compiled by the Board from these Account Currents.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the authority for amending the classification of accounts?

options.A: Amendments to the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account are issued by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas amendments and corrections to the railway classification of accounts contained in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through Correction Slips
options.B: Both the Government List and the railway classification are amended by the Railway Board
options.C: Amendments to the Government List are issued by the Railway Board, whereas the railway classification is amended by the Controller General of Accounts
options.D: Both the lists are amended by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India

e: Amendments to the Government List of Major and Minor Heads of Account are issued by the Controller General of Accounts, whereas amendments to the railway classification of accounts in the Finance Code are issued by the Railway Board through Correction Slips.

q: In the railway accounts, which of the following correctly distinguishes a debit balance from a credit balance under the suspense head 'Cheques and Bills'?

options.A: A debit balance represents cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank, whereas a credit balance represents cheques received but not yet realised
options.B: Both debit and credit balances under the head represent cheques issued by the Railways
options.C: A debit balance represents the cash balance of the Railways with the bank, whereas a credit balance represents cheques issued but not yet paid
options.D: A debit balance represents cheques and bills received but not yet realised (credited) by the bank, whereas a credit balance represents cheques issued but not yet paid by the bank

e: Under 'Cheques and Bills', a debit balance represents cheques and bills received but not yet realised (credited) by the bank, whereas a credit balance represents cheques issued by the Railways but not yet paid by the bank.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund are charged to the working expenses of the Railways as provided in the Budget, whether or not there is a surplus.
2. Appropriations to the Development Fund and the Capital Fund are made out of the surplus (net revenue) actually available at the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and Pension Fund are charged to working expenses as budgeted, whether or not there is a surplus. Appropriations to the Development Fund and Capital Fund come only from the surplus actually available at the year's close.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. In the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways, the actual expenditure is compared separately with the grants voted by Parliament and with the appropriations for expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. A saving available under the charged portion of a grant can be utilised, by re-appropriation, to meet an excess under the voted portion of the same grant.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: in the Appropriation Accounts, actual expenditure is compared separately with the voted grants and with the appropriations for charged expenditure. Statement 2 is false: a saving under the charged portion cannot be re-appropriated to meet an excess under the voted portion.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under the departmentalised system of accounting introduced in 1976, the accounts of most Ministries of the Government of India are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts through the Pay and Accounts Offices.
2. The Railways were kept outside this arrangement and compile their accounts themselves through their own accounts organisation.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: under the departmentalised system introduced in 1976, the accounts of most Ministries are compiled by the Controller General of Accounts through the Pay and Accounts Offices, while the Railways were kept outside the arrangement and compile their own accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The net result of apportionment of earnings for a zonal railway is adjusted through transfer transactions with the other railways concerned.
2. Apportionment involves an actual remittance of cash by the collecting railway to each of the other railways over which the traffic has passed.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct: the net result of apportionment for a zonal railway is adjusted through transfer transactions with the other railways concerned. Statement 2 is false: apportionment is a book adjustment and involves no actual remittance of cash.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The capital (principal) component of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation is charged under Plan Head 22.
2. The interest (finance charge) component of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation is charged to the revenue working expenses of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct: the capital (principal) component of the lease charges payable to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation is charged under Plan Head 22, while the interest (finance charge) component is charged to the revenue working expenses.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Every withdrawal from the balances of the Railway Funds, such as the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Development Fund, requires a separate appropriation by Parliament.
2. The balances of the Railway Funds are held in the Public Account of India and do not lapse at the close of the financial year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: withdrawals from the balances of the Railway Funds do not require a separate appropriation by Parliament. Statement 2 is correct: the fund balances are held in the Public Account of India and do not lapse at the close of the financial year.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A cut motion can be moved in the Lok Sabha in respect of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India.
2. Expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India can be discussed in Parliament, though it is not submitted to the vote of Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: a cut motion cannot be moved in respect of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, since cut motions relate only to Demands for Grants. Statement 2 is correct: charged expenditure can be discussed in Parliament though it is not voted.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The approximate earnings of the Railways are compiled only once, at the close of the financial year.
2. The accounted earnings are the final figures of earnings brought to account after internal check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: approximate earnings are compiled at short intervals throughout the year, not only once at its close. Statement 2 is correct: accounted earnings are the final figures brought to account after internal check and apportionment, as compiled in the Traffic Book.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The surrender of anticipated savings out of a sanctioned grant requires the approval of Parliament.
2. The amount of a grant sanctioned by Parliament can be increased during the year only through a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: surrender of anticipated savings out of a grant is an executive act and requires no approval of Parliament. Statement 2 is correct: a grant can be increased during the year only through a Supplementary Grant voted by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Sundry Other Earnings of the Railways are apportioned among the zonal railways in proportion to the distance over which the traffic is carried.
2. The earnings of local traffic, which both originates and terminates on the same railway, are retained wholly by that railway.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: Sundry Other Earnings are not apportioned among the zonal railways at all. Statement 2 is correct: earnings of local traffic, which originates and terminates on the same railway, are retained wholly by that railway.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.
2. The Appropriation Accounts and the Finance Accounts of the Railways are prepared from the accounts of the financial year after their closure.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is false: the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways are prepared by the Railways themselves, not by the Comptroller and Auditor General, who audits them. Statement 2 is correct: the Appropriation Accounts and Finance Accounts are prepared from the accounts of the financial year after their closure.

q: The original grant under a Demand is Rs 1,500 crore. During the year, supplementary grants of Rs 60 crore and Rs 40 crore are obtained in two batches and funds of Rs 75 crore are surrendered. The Final Grant for the Demand is:

options.A: Rs 1,465 crore
options.B: Rs 1,575 crore
options.C: Rs 1,525 crore
options.D: Rs 1,600 crore

e: Working: Final Grant = 1,500 + 60 + 40 - 75 = Rs 1,525 crore.

q: The Final Grant under a Demand for a year is Rs 850 crore and the actual expenditure booked against the Demand is Rs 884 crore. The excess expenditure, expressed as a percentage of the Final Grant, is:

options.A: 2 per cent
options.B: 5 per cent
options.C: 10 per cent
options.D: 4 per cent

e: Working: Excess expenditure = 884 - 850 = Rs 34 crore. Excess as percentage of Final Grant = 34/850 x 100 = 4 per cent.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 36,000 are to be apportioned among Railways A, B, C and D in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 900 km, 600 km, 300 km and 200 km respectively. The share of Railway B is:
e: Working: Total distance = 900 + 600 + 300 + 200 = 2,000 km. Share of Railway B = 36,000 x 600/2,000 = Rs 10,800.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 21,000 are to be apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 650 km, 450 km and 300 km respectively. The share of Railway X is:
e: Working: Total distance = 650 + 450 + 300 = 1,400 km. Share of Railway X = 21,000 x 650/1,400 = Rs 9,750.

q: The sanctioned cost of a work is Rs 900 crore. Expenditure of Rs 560 crore has been incurred on it up to the end of the previous year and the throw-forward of the work at the end of the current year will be Rs 200 crore. The outlay provided for the work in the current year is:

options.A: Rs 120 crore
options.B: Rs 160 crore
options.C: Rs 200 crore
options.D: Rs 140 crore

e: Working: Outlay in the current year = Sanctioned cost - Expenditure already incurred - Throw-forward = 900 - 560 - 200 = Rs 140 crore.

q: The annual plan outlay of the Railways is Rs 4,00,000 crore. It is financed by internal resources of Rs 80,000 crore and Extra Budgetary Resources of Rs 1,20,000 crore. The Gross Budgetary Support provided for the outlay is:

options.A: Rs 2,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 1,80,000 crore
options.C: Rs 2,20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 2,40,000 crore

e: Working: Gross Budgetary Support = Plan outlay - Internal resources - Extra Budgetary Resources = 4,00,000 - 80,000 - 1,20,000 = Rs 2,00,000 crore.

q: The gross earnings of the Railways for a year are Rs 6,400 crore and the total working expenses, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, are Rs 5,900 crore. The surplus (net revenue) available for the year is:

options.A: Rs 400 crore
options.B: Rs 450 crore
options.C: Rs 550 crore
options.D: Rs 500 crore

e: Working: Surplus (net revenue) = Gross earnings - Total working expenses = 6,400 - 5,900 = Rs 500 crore.

q: The opening debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' of a railway is Rs 240 lakh. During the year, stores of Rs 960 lakh are received into stock and stores of Rs 1,050 lakh are issued from stock. The closing debit balance under Stores Suspense is:

options.A: Rs 120 lakh
options.B: Rs 180 lakh
options.C: Rs 210 lakh
options.D: Rs 150 lakh

e: Working: Closing debit balance = Opening balance + Receipts into stock - Issues from stock = 240 + 960 - 1,050 = Rs 150 lakh.

q: The opening balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense' of a railway, representing the cost of jobs in progress, is Rs 80 lakh. During the year, jobs of Rs 420 lakh are charged to the head and completed jobs of Rs 460 lakh are transferred out of it. The closing balance under Manufacturing Suspense is:

options.A: Rs 40 lakh
options.B: Rs 60 lakh
options.C: Rs 80 lakh
options.D: Rs 20 lakh

e: Working: Closing balance = Opening balance + Jobs charged - Completed jobs transferred out = 80 + 420 - 460 = Rs 40 lakh, representing the cost of jobs still in progress.

q: The annual allotment for a head of account is Rs 1,600 crore and the budget proportion fixed for the first half of the year is 45 per cent. The proportionate allotment available for the first half of the year is:

options.A: Rs 640 crore
options.B: Rs 800 crore
options.C: Rs 720 crore
options.D: Rs 880 crore

e: Working: Proportionate allotment = 45 per cent of Rs 1,600 crore = Rs 720 crore.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 6,400 are to be apportioned between Railway M, over which the traffic travels 520 km, and Railway N, over which it travels 280 km. Apportionment being made in proportion to the distance travelled, the share of Railway M is:
e: Working: Total distance = 520 + 280 = 800 km. Share of Railway M = 6,400 x 520/800 = Rs 4,160.

q: Transfer transactions which involve no financial effect are intimated to the respondent railway through:

options.A: A Transfer Certificate
options.B: A TWFA advice
options.C: An Advice of Internal Check
options.D: A Cash Remittance Note

e: Transfer transactions involving no cash or financial effect are not sent by Transfer Certificate or Cash Remittance Note; they are intimated to the respondent railway through a TWFA advice, that is, a Transfer Without Financial Adjustment advice.

q: A debit balance under the suspense head 'PAO Suspense' represents:

options.A: Amounts paid or adjusted by the Railways on behalf of other Ministries/Departments, pending settlement or recovery from the Pay and Accounts Office concerned
options.B: Amounts received on behalf of other Ministries, pending payment to them
options.C: The cash balance of the Railways held with the Reserve Bank
options.D: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet paid by the bank

e: PAO Suspense is debited when the Railways pay or adjust amounts on behalf of other Ministries or Departments. A debit balance therefore means amounts pending settlement or recovery from the Pay and Accounts Office concerned.

q: A credit balance under the suspense head 'PAO Suspense' represents:

options.A: Amounts recoverable from other Ministries/Departments
options.B: Pension payments awaiting disbursement to pensioners
options.C: Amounts received or credited on behalf of other Ministries/Departments, pending payment or adjustment to them
options.D: Traffic earnings awaiting apportionment among railways

e: PAO Suspense is credited when amounts are received or credited on behalf of other Ministries or Departments. A credit balance therefore means amounts held pending payment or adjustment to the Ministry or Department concerned.

q: A debit balance under the suspense head 'AG Suspense' represents:

options.A: Amounts due to State Governments, pending remittance
options.B: The balance under 'Deposits with Reserve Bank'
options.C: Station earnings in transit to the bank
options.D: Amounts paid by the Railways on behalf of State Governments/Accountants General, pending recovery or settlement

e: AG Suspense is debited for payments made by the Railways on behalf of State Governments or Accountants General. A debit balance thus represents amounts pending recovery or settlement from them.

q: A credit balance under the suspense head 'AG Suspense' represents:

options.A: Amounts paid on behalf of State Governments, pending recovery
options.B: Amounts received or collected by the Railways for State Governments/Accountants General, pending remittance or adjustment
options.C: Loans raised by the Railways from the market
options.D: Wages drawn but remaining unpaid at the end of the month

e: AG Suspense is credited for amounts received or collected by the Railways for State Governments or Accountants General. A credit balance therefore represents amounts pending remittance or adjustment to them.

q: A debit balance under the suspense head 'PSB Suspense' represents:

options.A: Cheques deposited with the bank but not yet realised
options.B: Amounts credited by the bank to the Railways' account, pending advice
options.C: Payments made by the accredited public sector bank on behalf of the Railways, pending receipt of the bank's advice and adjustment to the final heads
options.D: Amounts due from stations on account of traffic transactions

e: PSB Suspense is debited when the accredited public sector bank makes payments on behalf of the Railways. A debit balance means such payments are pending receipt of the bank advice and adjustment to the final heads.

q: A credit balance under the suspense head 'PSB Suspense' represents:

options.A: Amounts credited by the accredited public sector bank to the Railways' account, pending the bank's advice and adjustment in the railway books
options.B: Payments made by the bank on behalf of the Railways, pending advice
options.C: Cheques issued by the Railways but not yet paid
options.D: Cash held in the chest of the Cash Office

e: PSB Suspense is credited when the accredited public sector bank credits amounts to the Railways account. A credit balance means such credits are pending the bank advice and adjustment in the railway books.

q: A debit balance under the suspense head 'Traffic Suspense' represents:

options.A: Earnings due to other railways, pending apportionment
options.B: Cash collected at stations and held in station chests
options.C: Amounts held on behalf of stations, pending disbursement
options.D: Debits raised against stations or other railways, such as disallowances and undercharges, pending recovery or final adjustment

e: Traffic Suspense is debited for debits raised against stations or other railways, such as disallowances and undercharges. A debit balance therefore represents amounts pending recovery or final adjustment.

q: A credit balance under the suspense head 'Traffic Suspense' represents:

options.A: Debits raised against stations, pending recovery
options.B: Traffic amounts and earnings held pending apportionment or adjustment in favour of the stations or other railways concerned
options.C: The value of stores held in stock in depots
options.D: Advances made to contractors, pending adjustment

e: Traffic Suspense is credited for traffic amounts and earnings held on behalf of stations or other railways. A credit balance therefore represents amounts pending apportionment or adjustment in their favour.

q: The debit side of the head 'Cheques and Bills', representing cheques and bills received and deposited with the bank, is cleared when:

options.A: A cheque is issued by the Cash & Pay Office
options.B: A bill is passed for payment by the Accounts Office
options.C: The bank intimates the realisation, or credit, of the cheques and bills deposited with it
options.D: The payee presents the cheque at his own bank

e: Cheques and bills deposited with the bank are debited to Cheques and Bills on receipt. The debit is cleared only when the bank intimates realisation or credit of those cheques and bills.

q: Works of passenger and other railway user amenities are financed from the subdivision of the Development Fund known as:

options.A: DF-I
options.B: DF-II
options.C: DF-III
options.D: The Capital Fund

e: Under the Development Fund subdivisions, DF-I is for passenger and other railway user amenities. Such works are therefore financed from DF-I, not from DF-II, DF-III or the Capital Fund.

q: Unremunerative operational improvement works on the Railways are financed from:

options.A: DF-I of the Development Fund
options.B: DF-II of the Development Fund
options.C: Capital in all cases
options.D: DF-III of the Development Fund

e: Under the Development Fund subdivisions, DF-III covers unremunerative operational improvement works. DF-I is for passenger amenities and DF-II for labour welfare, so unremunerative improvements fall under DF-III.

q: In the accounts of the Government of India, the Public Account of India forms:

options.A: Part I of the Government accounts
options.B: Part II of the Government accounts
options.C: Part III of the Government accounts
options.D: A section of the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Government accounts are kept in three parts: Part I Consolidated Fund, Part II Contingency Fund and Part III Public Account. The Public Account of India therefore forms Part III.

q: The balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense', representing the cost of jobs in progress in workshops, is exhibited in the Balance Sheet of the Railways as part of:

options.A: The Railway Pension Fund
options.B: The Block Account, on the assets side
options.C: The working expenses of the year
options.D: The Traffic Suspense account

e: Manufacturing Suspense represents the cost of jobs in progress in workshops. As work in progress is a capital asset, its balance is exhibited in the Railway Balance Sheet as part of the Block Account on the assets side.

q: The Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament is appointed by:

options.A: The Speaker of the Lok Sabha
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Finance Minister
options.D: The Chairman of the Rajya Sabha

e: The Chairman of the Committee on Public Undertakings is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from among the members of the Committee elected from the Lok Sabha.

q: The members of the Estimates Committee of Parliament hold office for a term of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: One year
options.C: Two years
options.D: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha

e: The Estimates Committee is constituted afresh every year. Its members hold office for a term of one year, though they may be re-elected.

q: The members of the Committee on Public Undertakings of Parliament hold office for a term of:

options.A: Five years
options.B: Three years
options.C: The remaining term of the Lok Sabha
options.D: One year

e: The Committee on Public Undertakings is also constituted every year on the Estimates Committee pattern. Its members hold office for a term of one year.

q: The reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President under Article ___ of the Constitution:
e: Under Article 151 of the Constitution, the reports of the Comptroller and Auditor General relating to the accounts of the Union are submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before Parliament.

q: The definition of a 'Money Bill' is contained in Article ___ of the Constitution:
e: Article 110 of the Constitution defines a Money Bill and lists the matters that can be included in it. Articles 109, 112 and 114 deal with procedure, the Annual Financial Statement and Appropriation Bills respectively.

q: Which of the following accounts is furnished as an annexure to the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways?

options.A: The Trial Balance
options.B: The Stock Adjustment Account
options.C: The Pink Book statement of works
options.D: The Suspense Register

e: The Stock Adjustment Account, showing price and quantity differences in stores adjusted during the year, is furnished as an annexure to the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways.

q: The principal advantage of E-Recon over the earlier paper-based system of transfer transactions is that:

options.A: Acceptance of transfers by the respondent railway is no longer necessary
options.B: Cash is physically transferred between railways more quickly
options.C: Statutory audit of transfer transactions is dispensed with
options.D: Transfer advices are transmitted electronically, enabling quicker matching of the originating and respondent entries

e: E-Recon transmits transfer advices electronically between railways instead of on paper. Its principal advantage is quicker matching of the originating entry with the respondent entry and faster acceptance and clearance.

q: Transfer transactions which remain unmatched or unaccepted under E-Recon:

options.A: Are written off automatically at the close of the month
options.B: Are converted into cash transactions with the Reserve Bank
options.C: Remain outstanding under the head 'Transfer Railways' and are pursued with the respondent railway till they are matched and accepted
options.D: Are transferred to the Railway Pension Fund

e: A transfer that is unmatched or unaccepted under E-Recon is not written off or converted into cash. It remains outstanding under Transfer Railways and is pursued with the respondent railway till it is matched and accepted.

q: The apportioned earnings of a zonal railway for a period exceed the earnings originated and collected by that railway. The net result of apportionment for that railway is:

options.A: A net credit due to that railway, adjusted through transfer transactions with the other railways concerned
options.B: A net debit against that railway, adjusted through transfer transactions
options.C: Nil, the excess lapsing to the Railway Board
options.D: A credit to the Development Fund of that railway

e: Apportionment divides through-traffic earnings among the railways that carried the traffic. If a railway's apportioned share exceeds what it originated and collected, the excess is a net credit due to it, settled by transfer transactions with the other railways.

q: Re-appropriation of funds between two works falling under the same Plan Head, within the same grant, can be sanctioned by:

options.A: The Railway Board only
options.B: The General Manager of the zonal railway, with the concurrence of the associated finance
options.C: The Divisional Railway Manager alone
options.D: The Principal Financial Adviser alone

e: Re-appropriation within the same grant and same Plan Head is within the powers of the General Manager of the zonal railway, exercised with the concurrence of the associated finance. It does not require Railway Board sanction.

q: Re-appropriation of funds from one Sub-Major Head to another Sub-Major Head under Major Head 3002, the Sub-Major Head being the unit of appropriation for revenue expenditure, requires the sanction of:

options.A: The General Manager of the zonal railway
options.B: The Divisional Railway Manager
options.C: The Principal Financial Adviser of the zonal railway
options.D: The Railway Board

e: For revenue expenditure under Major Head 3002, the Sub-Major Head is the unit of appropriation voted by Parliament. Re-appropriation from one Sub-Major Head to another therefore needs Railway Board sanction and cannot be done at zonal level.

q: At the level of the Government of India, exchequer control over expenditure is exercised through:

options.A: The Railway Board
options.B: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.C: The Ministry of Finance, keeping watch over the cash position of the Government with the Reserve Bank of India
options.D: The Estimates Committee of Parliament

e: Exchequer control at Government of India level is exercised by the Ministry of Finance, which watches the cash position of Government with the Reserve Bank of India and regulates releases and expenditure against that position.

q: The Cash Office of a zonal railway, on receiving the earnings remitted by stations, checks the remittances with reference to:

options.A: The Cash Remittance Notes accompanying the remittances
options.B: The Station Balance Sheets rendered to the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: The Transfer Certificates received from other railways
options.D: The Pink Book of the railway

e: The Cash Office receives station earnings with Cash Remittance Notes. It checks each remittance against the Cash Remittance Note accompanying it before accounting for the amount received.

q: The Approximate Account Current, rendered by zonal railways in the earlier practice, served mainly to:

options.A: Replace the final monthly account altogether
options.B: Furnish the Railway Board with approximate figures of the month's transactions in advance, pending the final compilation of the account
options.C: Report only the balances under the suspense heads
options.D: Obtain the supplementary grant for the month

e: The Approximate Account Current gave the Railway Board advance approximate figures of the month's transactions before the final accounts were compiled. It did not replace the final monthly account.

q: Materials released from a work of renewal and replacement are accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting their value to Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Ignoring them in the accounts of the work
options.C: Debiting their value to Capital as a fresh asset
options.D: Crediting their value to the renewal work concerned, thereby reducing the charge to the Depreciation Reserve Fund

e: Materials released from a renewal or replacement work have residual value. That value is credited to the renewal work itself, reducing the net charge borne by the Depreciation Reserve Fund for the work.

q: The corpus of the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) was made up of:

options.A: The safety surcharge on passenger fares alone
options.B: Market borrowings raised through the Indian Railway Finance Corporation alone
options.C: A contribution from the General Revenues (Ministry of Finance) together with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares
options.D: Appropriations made from the Railway Pension Fund

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was built up from two sources: a contribution from General Revenues through the Ministry of Finance and the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares. Neither source alone formed the whole corpus.

q: The second batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the:

options.A: Budget Session
options.B: Winter Session
options.C: Monsoon Session
options.D: A special session convened for the purpose

e: Supplementary Demands are presented in three batches in a year. The second batch is ordinarily presented in the Winter Session, the first in the Monsoon Session and the third in the following Budget Session.

q: 'CIPS' in the railway payment system is associated with:

options.A: Centralised electronic payment of bills and other payments across the Railways through the accredited bank
options.B: Computerised reservation of passenger accommodation
options.C: Apportionment of through-traffic earnings
options.D: Electronic auction of stores purchases

e: CIPS is the centralised system for electronic payment of bills and other payments across the Railways through the accredited bank. It is a payment system, not a reservation, apportionment or auction system.

q: Part A of the Traffic Book deals with the apportionment of Coaching earnings, which comprise:

options.A: Goods earnings and Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: Passenger earnings only
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings only
options.D: Passenger earnings and Other Coaching earnings

e: Part A of the Traffic Book apportions Coaching earnings. Coaching earnings comprise Passenger earnings and Other Coaching earnings, including parcels, luggage and cloak room receipts; Goods and Sundry earnings are dealt with separately.

q: The cost of repairs carried out by one zonal railway on the rolling stock of another zonal railway is adjusted between the two railways:

options.A: By daily remittance of cash by the debtor railway
options.B: Out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.C: Through transfer transactions, without any movement of cash between the railways
options.D: Through the Traffic Suspense account only

e: Repairs done by one railway on another railway's rolling stock involve no cash movement between railways. The cost is adjusted through transfer transactions, the repairing railway raising a debit on the owning railway.

q: Where the respondent railway does not agree with a debit raised against it through a Transfer Certificate, the correct course for it is to:

options.A: Pay the amount immediately and claim a refund later
options.B: Return the Transfer Certificate with its objections, the item remaining outstanding till the matter is settled
options.C: Write off the amount with the sanction of its General Manager
options.D: Charge the amount to its ordinary working expenses

e: A respondent railway that disputes a debit in a Transfer Certificate does not pay or write it off. It returns the certificate with its objections, and the item stays outstanding till the dispute is settled.

q: In an election year, along with the Interim Budget presented to Parliament, a Vote on Account is taken in order to:

options.A: Authorise expenditure for the initial part of the financial year, pending the presentation of the full Budget by the new Government
options.B: Regularise the excess expenditure of the previous year
options.C: Approve the Appropriation Accounts of the Railways
options.D: Sanction new services for the whole financial year

e: In an election year the Interim Budget is supported by a Vote on Account. It authorises expenditure for the initial part of the financial year till the new Government presents the full Budget and the Demands are voted.

q: The remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' in the railway books normally shows:

options.A: A credit balance
options.B: A nil balance at the close of every day
options.C: A balance only in the March accounts
options.D: A debit balance, representing the remittances made into the bank which are awaiting credit by the bank

e: Remittances into Banks records amounts remitted into the bank but not yet credited by it. It therefore normally shows a debit balance representing remittances awaiting bank credit.

q: In the railway accounts, the expression 'Debt Heads' is used collectively for:

options.A: The revenue heads of account only
options.B: The capital heads of account only
options.C: The debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads of account
options.D: The earnings heads of account

e: Debt Heads is the collective term in railway accounts for the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads. These heads carry balances forward, unlike revenue and capital heads which close each year.

q: Which of the following is NOT a permissible use of the Depreciation Reserve Fund?

options.A: Renewal and replacement of track
options.B: Construction of a new railway line
options.C: Renewal and replacement of bridges
options.D: Renewal and replacement of rolling stock

e: The Depreciation Reserve Fund finances renewal and replacement of existing assets such as track, bridges and rolling stock. Construction of a new line is a new asset charged to Capital, so it is not a permissible use of DRF.

q: The replacement of over-aged signalling equipment, being a safety-related renewal, is financed on the Railways from:

options.A: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh
options.B: The Development Fund
options.C: The Railway Pension Fund
options.D: The Debt Service Fund

e: Safety-related renewals such as replacement of over-aged signalling equipment are financed from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh, the fund created for safety works including renewals, replacements and safety projects.

q: Licence fees realised from catering units and book stalls at railway stations are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Passenger earnings
options.B: Goods earnings
options.C: Other Coaching Earnings
options.D: Sundry Other Earnings

e: Licence fees from catering units and book stalls are not traffic earnings from carriage. They are miscellaneous receipts classified under Sundry Other Earnings in the railway accounts.

q: The reports of the Public Accounts Committee of Parliament are presented to:

options.A: The Rajya Sabha only
options.B: The President of India
options.C: The Lok Sabha
options.D: The Finance Minister

e: The Public Accounts Committee is a committee of Parliament whose reports are presented to the Lok Sabha. Its examination is based on the Appropriation Accounts and the audit reports of the CAG.

q: The budget estimates prepared by the divisions and other field units of a zonal railway are, before submission to the Railway Board:

options.A: Sent directly by each division to the Railway Board
options.B: Consolidated and scrutinised at the headquarters of the zonal railway
options.C: Audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: Approved by the Ministry of Finance

e: Divisional and field unit estimates are not sent straight to the Railway Board. They are consolidated and scrutinised at zonal headquarters, and the zonal railway then submits its consolidated budget to the Board.

q: The distribution of the budget allotment among the divisions and units of a zonal railway is made with reference to the units of appropriation, namely:

options.A: Sub-Major Heads for revenue expenditure and Plan Heads for capital (works) expenditure
options.B: Primary Units for both revenue and capital expenditure
options.C: Plan Heads for revenue expenditure and Sub-Major Heads for capital expenditure
options.D: Detailed Heads for both revenue and capital expenditure

e: Budget allotments are distributed with reference to the units of appropriation: Sub-Major Heads for revenue expenditure and Plan Heads for capital or works expenditure. Primary and Detailed Heads are lower levels of classification.

q: Earnings of the PRS/UTS systems transferred electronically by the accredited bank, but not yet credited to the Railways' account at the close of the day, are shown in the railway accounts as:

options.A: Sundry Other Earnings
options.B: A credit balance under Traffic Suspense
options.C: Deposits with Reserve Bank
options.D: Cash-in-Transit

e: PRS and UTS earnings transferred electronically by the bank but not yet credited to the Railways account at day end are in transit between the bank and the Railways. They are shown as Cash-in-Transit in the accounts.

q:
Consider the following statements about the Trial Balance extracted from the books of a railway:
1. An error of complete omission of a transaction is not disclosed by the Trial Balance.
2. A compensating error, in which one error is offset by another of equal amount, is not disclosed by the Trial Balance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: A Trial Balance only checks arithmetical agreement of debits and credits. A complete omission affects neither side, and compensating errors cancel each other, so neither error is disclosed by the Trial Balance. Both statements are correct.

q: The Journal Proper of a railway is used for recording:

options.A: Entries which are not recorded in any other subsidiary book, such as opening, closing and adjustment entries
options.B: All cash receipts and payments of the Cash & Pay Office
options.C: The traffic transactions of stations
options.D: Only the transactions of the Railway Board's office

e: The Journal Proper records entries that find no place in any other subsidiary book, such as opening, closing, transfer and adjustment entries. Cash, traffic and other routine transactions are recorded in their own books.

q: The Cash Book maintained in the railway accounts has a dual character, in that it is:

options.A: Both a General Book and an Appropriation Account
options.B: Both a Journal and a Trial Balance
options.C: Both a subsidiary record and a Debt Head Report
options.D: Both a book of original entry and a ledger account for cash

e: The Cash Book is a book of original entry in which cash transactions are first recorded, and it also functions as the ledger account for cash itself. It thus has the dual character of a journal and a ledger account.

q: The Balance Sheet of the Railways is correctly described as:

options.A: A statement of the balances standing in the General Books, exhibiting the assets and liabilities of the Railways
options.B: An account in the Ledger, debited and credited like other accounts
options.C: A part of the monthly Account Current rendered to the Railway Board
options.D: A statement of the earnings of the year only

e: The Balance Sheet of the Railways is a statement, not a ledger account. It sets out the balances in the General Books so as to exhibit the assets and liabilities of the Railways at the close of the period.

q:
Consider the following statements about the closing of the annual accounts:
1. Balances under the debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads are carried forward from one financial year to the next.
2. The revenue and capital expenditure heads of a year are closed at the end of that year and do not leave balances to be carried forward.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Debt, deposit, suspense and remittance heads carry their balances forward year to year till cleared. Revenue and capital heads of a year are closed at year end against the grant and leave no balance. Both statements are correct.
